title: Strict drop of residue transcendence degree under specialization
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For any distinct points $x,x^{\prime}\in X$ with $x^{\prime}\in\overline{\{x\}}$, one has $$\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x)>\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(x^{\prime}).$$ The fields $\kappa(x)$ and $\kappa(x^{\prime})$ and their $k$-structures are the residue fields of [def-weil-residue-field], and transcendence degree is [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Closure is in the Zariski topology. No quasi-compactness, reducedness, or separation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06RU (lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization), assertion (3), with base Spec k.

proof.text: By the definition of locally finite type, choose an affine member $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the finite-type affine cover of $f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}k)=X$ containing $x^{\prime}$. Thus $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Since $x^{\prime}\in\overline{\{x\}}$, every open containing $x^{\prime}$ contains $x$: otherwise that open would be disjoint from $\{x\}$. In particular $x\in U$. The affine-open identification gives distinct prime ideals $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$ of $A$ representing $x,x^{\prime}$.

source.place: lemma-dimension-fibre-specialization, affine reduction for assertion (3); locally finite type as in definition-locally-finite-type

proof.text: The closed sets of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ are $V(I)=\{\mathfrak r:I\subseteq\mathfrak r\}$. Consequently the closure of the point $\mathfrak p$ is $V(\mathfrak p)$: it is closed and contained in every closed set containing $\mathfrak p$. Restricting closure to the open subspace $U$ therefore gives $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q$. Set $B=A/\mathfrak p$ and $C=A/\mathfrak q$. They are nonzero domains since the two ideals are prime, and finite type over $k$ since the images of any finite algebra-generating family for $A$ generate each quotient.

source.place: lemma-tr-deg-specialization, reduction to the two prime quotients; Zariski closed sets defined in section-spectrum

proof.text: Apply clauses (1) and (2) of the affine residue-field theorem at both points. They identify $\kappa_X(x)$ with a fraction field of $B$ and $\kappa_X(x^{\prime})$ with a fraction field of $C$, compatibly with the maps from $A$. These identifications respect $k$: in each case the structure map is the composite $k\to A\to\kappa_X(z)$ induced by $f|_U$, and the affine identification commutes with its second arrow. Thus the transcendence degrees in the item are those of these two fraction fields with their induced $k$-structures.

source.place: Local rings, paragraph identifying the residue field at a prime with the fraction field of its quotient; schemes.tex, discussion before lemma-characterize-points

proof.text: The finite-type domain dimension theorem applies to $B$ and $C$: both are domains of finite type over the field $k$ by step 2. It gives finite natural numbers $d=\dim B=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(x)$ and $e=\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(x^{\prime})$, using the compatible fraction-field identifications of step 3.

source.place: Tag 00P0, lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring, as used in lemma-tr-deg-specialization

proof.text: Because $C$ is a nonzero domain and its prime-chain lengths have finite supremum $e$, there is a chain $\mathfrak r_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak r_e$ of primes in $C$ (a bounded nonempty subset of $\mathbf N$ attains its supremum). Take inverse images under the surjection $B\to C$: they are prime because their quotients are the domains $C/\mathfrak r_i$, and remain distinct because the map is surjective. Each contains the nonzero prime $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak p$ of $B$. Prepending the zero prime of the domain $B$ therefore gives a strict prime chain in $B$ of length $e+1$. By the definition of Krull dimension, $e+1\le d$, hence $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(x^{\prime})<\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(x)$ as required.

source.place: lemma-tr-deg-specialization, final dimension inequality, expanded as a prime-chain argument
